### Method 1: Force all git requests to HTTPS (Recommended, fastest)

If you don't want to modify the configuration file manually, you can directly run this global configuration command. It tells Git: Whenever it encounters a `git@github.com:` address, it will automatically replace it with `https://github.com/`.

Run in the terminal:

Bash

```
git config --global url."https://github.com/".insteadOf git@github.com:
```

After running the above command, the update command to try again:

Bash

```
git submodule update --init --recursive
```

> **Note**: If the sub-module is a **private repo**, Git will prompt for the GitHub username and password (the current password usually refers to a **Personal Access Token**). If it is a public repo, it will be downloaded directly.

------

### Method 2: Manually modify the `.gitmodules` file

If you want to permanently modify the configuration of this project, you can edit the `.gitmodules` file in the root directory of the project.

1. Edit the file:

Open .gitmodules using vim or nano:

   Bash

   ```
   vim .gitmodules
   ```

2. Modify the URL:

   Find the section [submodule "policy"], and change the url from SSH format to HTTPS format.

   **Before modification:**

   Ini, TOML

   ```
   url = git@github.com:shuosha/policy_training.git
   ```

   **Modified:**

   Ini, TOML

   ```
   url = https://github.com/shuosha/policy_training.git
   ```

3. Synchronize and update (key step):

After modifying the file, you must run `sync` for Git to recognize the new URL, and then update it:

   Bash

   ```
   git submodule sync
   git submodule update --init --recursive
   ```

------

### Method 3: Only modify the local git configuration (does not affect files)

If you don't want to modify the `.gitmodules` file in the code (to avoid affecting others when submitting), you can only modify the `.git/config` file.

1. Open the `.git/config` file:

   Bash

   ```
   vim .git/config
   ```

2. Find the `[submodule "policy"]` section and replace `url` with `https://github.com/shuosha/policy_training.git`.

3. Save and exit, then run the update command directly.

### Summary Recommendations

Since it is in the `root@gpufree-container` environment, I recommend using **Method 1** directly. It does not require modifying files through an editor, and it can immediately solve similar issues of all submodules.

Next step:

You can directly copy and run this command, then try the update again:

Bash

```
git config --global url."https://github.com/".insteadOf git@github.com: && git submodule update --init --recursive
```
